September 2009 ## A Modest Improvement in Outlook - As more data has become available we have made some small revisions to our H1 data and we now believe that the global copper wirerod market contracted by 11.4% rather than our previous estimate of 11.8%. It is now clear that all the major markets around the world have stabilised and that China is leading the recovery. At present it looks as if the early stages of a global recovery should start to be seen in Q3, with improving year-on-year comparisons, but there is still a significant risk that there will be a second dip to this recession, although the chance of this happening is receding. - Global consumption of winding wire fell by 16.4% in H1, which made it the worst performing sector. This product sector is typically the first to emerge from a recession so the fact that a number of manufacturers making winding wire are reporting a modest upturn in demand is a further positive sign that we are entering the early stages of a recovery. - Despite relatively low copper demand the price of copper has continued to rise, driven by large imports of refined copper into China. Whilst the high price has implications in terms of cash flow for the cable industry, the unexpected strength in the copper price has helped limit the fall in cable manufacturers’ sales value. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 September 2009 Copper wire, cable and wirerod **www.crugroup.com** # Europe Our figures show that copper wirerod production in Europe totalled 731,000 tonnes in Q2, a decline of 23.8% y-o-y. Total copper wire and cable production amounted to 601,000 tonnes. This represents a 24.5% y-o-y decrease. Both figures are in line with our earlier estimates. CRU’s contacts reported that there is still no proved upturn in the market, which remains depressed especially due to the continued low level of construction activity and ongoing liquidity problems. A further disruption has been triggered by the rally in copper prices which has led to adjustments in price lists. ### **Tales from the marketplace** **UK** -based **Rautomead** installed and commissioned its third copper wirerod casting machine at **AB Electrokoppar** in **Sweden** . End-products will be small Cu-Ag rectangular wires and other profile shapes used in the automotive and other sectors. In **Italy, Enel** signed a protocol with the authorities in **Sicily** for the development of the island’s energy sector. The power company plans to invest €1 billion (US$1.4 billion) to develop new wind and solar plants. In **Russia** , **Furukawa Electric** concluded a technical assistance agreement with **Uncomtech** for the production of 110kV power cables. Sales are expected to commence in early 2010. ### **H1 results and comments from major players** **Draka’s** sales volume in H1 contracted by 20% while revenue was down by 30%. Sales to the Western European market in the same period shrank by 18-19%. The company reported that market conditions appear to be stabilising since Q2 but that the economic outlook remains uncertain. Draka intends to focus on halogen-free fire-resistance cables and those for special applications such as renewable energy systems. **Prysmian** saw its sales in H1 decrease by 18.3% y-o-y. The energy business alone fell by 17.6% y-o-y whilst that of telecom contracted by 24.1% y-o-y. Because the large utilities restarted work on new projects, the high voltage market reported signs of improvement in Q2. It is anticipated that in the trade and installers and power distribution businesses, as well as certain products in the industrial segment, weak demand will continue in H2. The company does not rule out the possibility th

at demand in businesses like trade and installers could experience another contraction in H2. An organic decrease in the H1 cable business of 16.4% was posted by **Nexans** . Some stabilisation was experienced in Q2 as the cable business rose by 1.7% q-o-q. In the same period, the energy infrastructure business increased by 10.1% q-o-q but the industry and building business dropped by 5% and 9.7% respectively. For the future, Nexans is looking to focus on cables for energy infrastructure. Having refocused on its cable business, electrical wire sales fell by 45.4% y-o-y in H1. Due to the low volume of activity in building, industry and private networks in Europe and North America, negative organic growth of 10-15% is expected for the whole of 2009. **NKT Cables** achieved 3% y-o-y organic growth in Q2 supported by the high voltage segment and railway catenary wires. But in the same period, the medium and low voltage segments suffered 20% and 15% y-o-y contraction respectively. For the nine months to June 2009, **Aurubis** announced an organic decrease of 21.3% y-o-y. The copper products business unit, which includes copper wirerod, continuous copper cast shapes, rolled copper products and specialty copper products, exhibited an organic decrease of 39.1% y-o-y. However, the company reported stabilisation in Europe since early summer. s seek to rundown inventory. Few of our contacts expect any significant improvement in volume demand in 2009 or even 2010, but most seem agreed that demand has found its floor. Wire and cable companies are focused on adjusting cost structure, capacity and inventory levels due to reduced sales levels. However, uncertainty about demand and prices has caused considerable volatility in pricing levels, and many wire and cable companies have seen lower margins. Encore Wire, for instance, reported that in Q2 the average price of wire increased 21% while copper prices increased 34%. Among the major companies, General Cable reported volumes down 19.8% y-o-y and down 2.2% on Q1. International Wire reported volumes down by 33.1% y-o-y. Encore Wire reported volumes down by 12.4% in the first six months of 2009, with Q2 2009 experiencing a 9% decline versus Q1. Weakness extended to the communication cables sector, with Commscope reporting lower volumes and declining sales in all product segments. ### **US commercial construction spending falls significantly** The outlook for the most important segment for US wire and cable demand remains very poor. Nonresidential construction has largely found its floor. Residential construction spending in July was up 2.3% m-o-m but down 26.9% y-o-y. However, with housing prices still very depressed and significant residential inventory still unsold, no quick recovery is expected. The biggest concern for US wire and cable companies, however, is the rapidly worsening fortunes of the non-residential construction sector, with several companies suggesting that wire and cable demand could weaken further next year as a result. US non-residential construction was down 2.6% y-o-y and 1.0% m-o-m in July, with private sector construction the worst affected. The American Institute of Architects has recently revised its forecasts for commercial construction. It expects that construction spending on offices, retail centers and hotels will fall by 16% this year and 12% in 2010. ### **Nexans sells Montreal wirerod mill to AmRod Corp** **Nexans** announced that it has signed an agreement to sell its Montreal wirerod mill to **AmRod Corp** , a copper wirerod producer based in New Jersey, USA. The closing of the transaction is scheduled to take place in Q4 2009, subject to a number of regulatory conditions. The sale is consistent with Nexans’ plan to reduce foreign sales of copper wirerod and focus on its core wire and cable businesses. forming sector has been power cable which has seen production fall by around 10% year-on-year in H1, although worryingly whilst other sectors have seen the fall in production stabilise or even rise a little in the last few months, output of power cable has continued to fall. In March the year-onyear fall in output was just 4.2%, but this grew to 13.9% in April and 25.6% in May. As a result of the poor performance of the power cable sector total May shipments of copper cable were down by 30% year-on-year at 41,600 tonnes conductor, which makes May the worst performing month of the current recession. Since then there has been a modest recovery in both June and July, with July production at the highest level for eight months, although it was still 21% down year-on-year. The fact that the automotive sector has shown a modest recovery in Q2 and the winding wire sector has now stabilised is good news, with these two sectors being leading indicators of a recovery. However, the weakness in the power cable sector shows that this recession is likely to be prolonged and that it will be well into 2010 before any strong recovery across the board is likely in Japan. 

### **South Korea confirmed as the best regional performer** 

As we noted in the last issue of this report, the South Korean cable industry has been much stronger in H1 of this year than most people expected. The bringing forward of many power cable orders and the continued strength of the shipbuilding and offshore cable sectors has underpinned a 14.8% growth in copper wirerod production and a 9.9% growth in copper wire and cable production. As well as domestic demand South Korea has seen exports hold up better than its neighbours. Taiwan has seen export volumes fall by over 50% in H1, with Japanese exports down by almost 30%, whilst for South Korea export volumes are around 22% lower. China is South Korea’s biggest export market accounting for around 30% of exports by volume. 

### **Taiwan sees a 30% fall in copper cable production in H1** 

Taiwan has been the hardest hit of all the countries in North East Asia with copper wirerod production falling by almost 25% year-on-year in H1 and copper cable production down by around 30%. All sectors of the cable industry have been hit with winding wire and electronic wire production down by around 40% in H1 and power and communication cable production falling by around 25%. Throughout Q2 the monthly fall in output volume was stable at around 25% lower than the corresponding months in 2008. There have been no clear signs of a recovery in any of the product sectors so it looks as if the market is bumping along the bottom at present.  Not surprisingly in the face of such poor demand, coupled with lower raw material prices, Taiwanese wire and cable company sales figures are sharply lower. # Rest of World 

### **All eyes remain on China** 

With the price of copper continuing to rise in a way that is seemingly at odds with the fundamentals of the market, all eyes are focused on China as its nominal consumption of copper surges. Implied consumption of refined copper in China in the first half of 2009 is almost 50% up on H1 2008, and the challenge is to understand how much of this copper is actually being consumed, and how much is being put into stocks or being held by speculators. As we have noted before some of the rise in consumption is down to a fall in consumption of scrap copper, but based on our analysis of the wire and cable market it is clear that a significant volume is also being stockpiled by the SRB and speculators, plus there is also an element of restocking through the supply chain in the anticipation of improving demand.  Our latest data shows that copper wirerod production grew by 7.4% year-on-year in H1 to almost 1.9 million tonnes. With lower imports, copper wirerod consumption was up by 4.9%, with a fall in consumption in Q1 of 3.8% being more than balanced out by a 13.6% rise in Q2. 

At a macro level the recent surge in investment is now translating into an upturn in activity and the industrial inventories-to-shipments ratio has returned to a more normal level, with industrial production rising by 10.8% year-on-year in July. The power cable sector remains strong driven by spending on infrastructure and other areas of strong demand are railway cables and ships cables (ship production was up 77.2% year-on-year in H1). Demand from the automotive sector has been boosted by Government incentives which have reduced purchase tax from 10% to 5% on cars with engines smaller than 1.6 litres and subsidies for rural households to scrap 3-wheelers and low speed trucks and purchase a new car or minivan. As a result vehicle production was up 16.6% in H1 and the rate of growth is rising with production up just over 50% in July. Production of domestic appliances is also being boosted by Government incentives with output of household washing machines, fridges and freezers up by over 20% year-on-year in June and July. After a fall of 15% in H1 production of air conditioners is now also starting to recover with growth in July of 9.8% over July 2008. There has also been a marked upturn in electricity generation in June and July, with growth of around 5% in each of these months after falling output for the first five months of the year. This is a further indication of a recovery in industrial production which should help boost demand for winding wire and energy cable. The construction sector is also looking much healthier with the year-on-year growth in floor space under construction reaching 36.3% in June, with residential construction up 41.3%.
